To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

blanket peat hillslopes have pipe frequencies that are controlled by land management practice (moorland griping) and topographic position, and that slope gradient is not an important control on pipe frequency. [2]
blanket peat pipes are found in all peatland catchments surveyed, and the frequency of pipes is strongly controlled by land management, topographic position, and annual precipitation. [1]
blanket peat pipe networks are ubiquitous, but their frequency varies in response to land use and topographic position. [2]
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a conceptual model for pipe development in blanket peat.
the development of a new conceptual model to explain the controls of soil pipe frequency and distribution in blanket peat hillslopes.
how the structure of blanket peat controls pipe network development, and the implications of this for land management. [2]
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
blanket peat pipe networks are controlled by land use, topography, and climate. [2]
blanket peat pipe frequencies are controlled by a complex interplay of peat structural properties, land management practice, topographic position and climate. [2]
blanket peat pipe network development is a complex process that is controlled by the interplay of several factors including slope position, land management, aspect, and precipitation. [2]
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pipe frequency increases from midslopes to footslopes to topslopes in blanket peats.
the frequency of soil pipe development in blanket peats is a function of the following: (a) land management (moor gripping); (b) hillslope position; (c) aspect; (d) precipitation. [2]
pipe frequency in blanket bogs is a function of land management, topographic position, and annual precipitation. [2]
The main takeaway from our work is that
soil pipes are ubiquitous in British upland peatlands and that they are strongly influenced by land management. [2]
blanket peats have a high propensity to pipe and that the frequency and distribution of piping is controlled by land management and topography.

blanket peat pipe network frequency can be predicted using a simple linear model that includes only two variables (slope position and management) and that this is the case in all but the driest blanket peatlands.
